stop_conditions: Claim 2608 ownership, reserved version 20260909005945, or coordinator route changes
Main moves in a way that invalidates the re-derived function bodies or the branch evidence
SQL scope widens beyond the two claimed functions, or any required check refuses
assumptions: Claim 2608 reserves version 20260909005945 and objects function public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups and function public.refresh_style_group_counts_batch; the second is over-declared and deliberately left untouched

public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups has no prior migration file; its body is re-derived from supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql rather than merged from a competing CREATE OR REPLACE
public.update_bulk_operation replaces the rebuild-style-groups object wholesale, so the reconcile marker must be a separate top-level BULK_OPERATIONS key
The worker-signalled variant of #2440 and the alert that consumes last_reconciled_at are PopDAM application work in another repository and are not claimed here
Contract tests were executed from empty on a disposable local PostgreSQL cluster built the CI way, and pass with the new body installed

The Database Contract Tests lane applies supabase/ci-bootstrap/010_pre_adoption_baseline.sql BETWEEN its two migration replay passes, so a migration that replaces a baseline routine and succeeds in pass 1 is overwritten by the baseline. This migration therefore deletes the baseline's copy of public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups, which is the remedy the baseline's own instructions name; the baseline grants are left as idempotent no-ops.

Review HIGH: the floor arm ran while the rebuild was queued/running because ARM 1 returns without seeding last_reconciled_at. Fixed by gating ARM 3 on the operation not being in flight, where in flight means status running/queued AND the operation touched inside the floor window. Seeding last_reconciled_at on the enqueue was rejected deliberately: that field is the detector answer to when the counts last refreshed, and stamping it on an enqueue would make the detector lie.
Review MEDIUM: ARM 2 is now evaluated before ARM 1, so the 06:00 enqueue cannot overwrite a completed-but-unreconciled run. Cost is at most a ten-minute enqueue delay on the poll that reconciles.

Review LOW (chunk walk is not one snapshot under READ COMMITTED): accepted and not changed. The walk exists precisely so the reconcile does not hold one long snapshot; a repeatable-read snapshot would reintroduce the long transaction and the bloat this design avoids, and a membership row inserted mid-walk is picked up by the next completed-run reconcile at most one rebuild later. Answered in the PR body rather than silently ignored.

Review LOW (authenticated retains EXECUTE): left in place, disclosed. The grant is pre-existing baseline ACL, no caller can be proven absent from this repository because the consumer PopDAM is a separate repository, and the contract test pins the grant set. The exposed surface is bounded: every arm is idempotent by run_id or by the floor, so an authenticated caller can force at most one recompute per completed run, which pg_cron would run anyway.
prohibited_actions: No preview apply, no merge, no production promotion, no review allocation
No shared database writes and no data seeding
No edit to any object outside claim 2608, and no edit to an already applied migration
No hand-picked migration version and no hand-edited claim block
goal: Stop the style-group asset-count reconcile running on the clock 2h15m before the rebuild that changes the membership it counts. Delete cron job nightly-reconcile-sg-asset-counts, turn nightly-rebuild-style-groups into a 10-minute poll, and rewrite public.queue_nightly_rebuild_style_groups as a three-armed driver: enqueue once per UTC day at or after 06:00 UTC, reconcile in 500-group chunks only when the rebuild reaches status completed with an unreconciled run_id, and reconcile unconditionally if the last one is older than 7 days so the new silent failure mode is bounded and observable. Generation 4 answers the slot-1 review: the floor arm no longer runs while the rebuild is in flight (the HIGH finding), the chained-reconcile condition is evaluated before the enqueue condition (the MEDIUM finding), and the contract file pins both, plus the staleness bound that keeps a dead worker from suppressing the floor forever.
